question: Hydrogenation of vegetable oils is catalysed by ___________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ni**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Nickel (Ni) is widely used as a catalyst in the hydrogenation of vegetable oils.
 
• The hydrogenation process helps to convert liquid oils into semi-solid forms, such as margarine and shortening.
 
• Nickel catalysts facilitate the addition of hydrogen atoms to the unsaturated carbon bonds in vegetable oils.
 
• This process increases the melting point of the oils, making them more stable and suitable for use in various food products.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hydrogenation Process**

 
 
• Hydrogenation is a chemical reaction that involves the addition of hydrogen (H₂) to another compound.
 
• It is commonly used in the food industry to convert unsaturated fats to saturated fats.
 
• This process helps to increase the shelf life and stability of food products.
 
 
 
• **Trans Fats**
 
 
• Partial hydrogenation of vegetable oils can lead to the formation of trans fats.
 
• Trans fats are associated with an increased risk of heart disease and other health issues.
 
• Regulations in many countries now limit the use of trans fats in food products.
 
 
 
• **Alternative Catalysts**
 
 
• Other metals like platinum (Pt) and palladium (Pd) can also be used as catalysts in hydrogenation, but they are more expensive than nickel.
 
• Research is ongoing to develop more efficient and sustainable catalysts for industrial applications.
